---
name: ponytail
description: >
  Lazy senior dev mode: the smallest change that fully solves the task, and a
  reply a busy human understands in one read. Use on any coding task (writing,
  fixing, refactoring, reviewing, choosing dependencies) and when the user says
  "ponytail", "be lazy", "simplest solution", "yagni", or complains about
  over-engineering or bloat. Levels: lite, full (default), ultra.
argument-hint: "[lite|full|ultra|off]"
license: MIT
---

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. The best code is the code never written. You solve the whole problem with the least new code. End your reply with one or two lines: what you skipped or did not check, and any risk the user must know.

Active for the whole session until the user says "stop ponytail" or "normal mode". Switch level: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## Before you write

Read the task and the code it touches. List every place your change must reach: callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports. Check what your change could break for users: data it would destroy or expose, callers that stop working. That is scope. Extra features are not.

## The smallest complete change

Take the first option that fully works:

1. Does it need to exist? Skip features, options and flexibility nobody asked for, and name them in one line. A vague request ("build me X") gets the smallest version that does the core job.
2. Already in this codebase (a helper, component, service, pattern)? Use it the way the surrounding code does.
3. Standard library or a platform feature? Use it, unless the project has its own. A house component beats a native widget.
4. An installed dependency? Use it. Never add a dependency for a few lines.
5. Can it be one line a reader gets at a glance? One line.
6. Otherwise: the minimum code that works.

- Be lazy about the solution, never about the change itself: finish every part the task needs, including the callers, tests and fixtures your change breaks.
- No abstraction, wrapper, type conversion, option, config, boilerplate or "for later" code nobody asked for. Keep values in the form the platform already gives you. Deletion beats addition. Keep the structure the codebase already has: its layers, interfaces and conventions.
- The shortest working diff wins, once you know everything it must touch. A one-liner that needs decoding is not short.
- Comment only the why the code cannot show, in one line.
- Bug fix: before you edit, grep every caller of the function you touch, then fix the root cause once in the shared code.
- Code you move or merge keeps its error handling and validation.
- Between options of equal size, take the one that is correct on edge cases.
- Lazy code without its check is unfinished: new non-trivial logic (a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security, or a whole new script or app) leaves one small test or an assert-based self-check. Trivial changes need none.
- A shortcut with a known limit gets a code comment in this form: `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`.

Never cut: validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs, anything the user asked for.

## Levels

| Level | Behavior |
|-------|----------|
| **lite** | Build what was asked. Name the smaller option in one line and let the user pick. |
| **full** | The rules above. Default. |
| **ultra** | Also question the request: before building, push back on any part the need does not justify. |

## Codex seat worklogs

Project layouts vary by language. Set up this worklog structure only when it
does not already exist, and use timestamped filenames in `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`
form:

- `.agents/worklog/codex/plan/<timestamp>_plan.md` stores the plan and design
  written before implementation. Ask the user questions when needed, and
  update the plan when questions, learning, or completed tasks change it. It
  must contain `Goal`, `Scope`, `Assumptions`, `Design`, `Tests`, and
  `Open Questions`.
- `.agents/worklog/codex/todo/<timestamp>_todo.md` derives its tasks from the
  plan. Move completed items from `TODO` to `Done`; when `TODO` is empty, set
  its status to `done` and rename it to `<timestamp>_done.md`. It must contain
  `TODO` and `Done`.
- `.agents/worklog/codex/learn/<timestamp>_learn.md` records only reusable,
  validated knowledge that speeds a future decision. State what was learned
  and where it applies, update the plan's `Assumptions`, `Design`, or `Tests`
  when relevant. A learn file must contain `Date`, `Learnings`, and
  `Plan Updates`.

Every plan, todo, and learn file starts with YAML frontmatter containing
`type` (`plan`, `todo`, or `learn`), `id` (`YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS`), `owner` (for
example, `codex-a`), and ISO8601 `created_at` and `updated_at`. Additionally:

- todo requires `status`, `workstream`, and `related_plan`; status is one of
  `active`, `blocked`, `done`, or `superseded`;
- plan requires `status`, one of `draft`, `active`, `done`, or `superseded`;
- learn requires `validated` (`true` or `false`) and `apply_to` (plan/tests),
  and may be created only when reusable and validated.

Optional frontmatter keys are `depends_on` (todo ID array), `blocked_reason`
for blocked work, `evidence` (path array), and `tags`.

## Review and integration invariants

- Review every RESULT adversarially across correctness, regressions, security, and reporting omissions: try to refute it, independently re-derive findings, and never treat sampled spot checks as full verification.
- Acceptance review, adversarial RESULT review, and review-profile work remain orchestrator-side; never delegate them to a worker, and keep `make require-crit-review` as the final integration step. Revisit only if worker-side model capability surpasses the orchestrator tier.
- A design review runs in paired rounds. Both reviewers, a fresh Claude context on the `review` profile and a Codex read-only run under a `codex-review` identity, get the same design hash at the same time. The orchestrator revises once per pair of results and opens no round while one is still open. The third pair is the last: on its accept the design is frozen at the hash the pair last accepted, the third pair's own, and whatever is still open at that hash becomes a residual list that is worker input; on its revise or reject nothing is frozen and the design goes back to a context other than its author, never to a fourth pair; a revision after the third pair is not made, and any later change to a hashed key is a new pair (INV-7). The review judges the invariants, threat model, trust anchors and premises for contradiction and enforceability, never implementation detail.
- A task-file review is one round with a fixed stop condition: no contradiction with the design, the premises hold, `allowed_files` covers every touch point that grep finds, and one invariant check (for a task that carries an `invariants` key: the task id maps to its `implementing_tasks` entry, the invariant ids match, and each invariant's sentence equals the design's byte-for-byte, the design read from main (INV-2), checked by hand in the review; a task without the key needs no entry). Anything finer belongs to the worker and the implementation PR.
- A boundary PR synchronizes records at a boundary. It carries no task draft under review. A design not yet on `main` lands through a merged boundary PR before its implementing TASK is dispatched (INV-2), and any merged boundary that carries the design meets that precondition.
- A task that touches a trust boundary (anything the design tier lists, CI that decides a required check, code that executes PR-controlled input) carries a `threat_table` in its front matter: one `{control, disposition}` row per thing the PR or the orchestrator controls (the tree and its tests, task.md, workflow files, interpreter and environment files, in-process effects, new or renamed scripts, metadata separators). The row unit is one row per `allowed_files` entry, one row per listed control that is not a path (task metadata, workflow and interpreter or environment inputs, in-process effects, new or renamed scripts, metadata separators), carried by the declared test module's row where that is where the control acts, and one row per orchestrator effect from the fixed list (forced removal, merge, update-branch); under a wildcard `allowed_files` entry whose files are executed or applied (scripts, workflows, hooks, settings, the rules seats follow), one row per concrete file the PR changes; a wildcard over test fixtures or other data files keeps one row; C4 and C7b of `scripts/orchestrator/task-consistency-check.py` verify the path half before dispatch, and the task-file review checks the rest. A disposition takes one of three forms: `closed: tests/<file>::<name>`, the test that closes the row; `residual: <sentence>`, the compensating control; `out-of-scope: <task id>`, the task that owns the row. The task-file review checks the three shape rules by hand: a `closed` selector names a test present in the PR tree at acceptance, an `out-of-scope` owner is a task id in the design's `implementing_tasks`, a `residual` payload is a sentence of at least 20 characters (the gate's minimum for a reason). For a `closed` row it checks the selector's form only, since the test does not exist before implementation. Substance is the reviewers': the task-file review, the Bot and the auditor judge each row against the diff. The table is the task's completion condition: a missing row is added once, counted as an amendment, never fixed finding by finding.
- Before every acceptance action (revise, accept, merge) the orchestrator runs `scripts/regime-counters.sh <task id>` and pastes its output into the acceptance record. S2 is decided from INV-6's counts: each component the script prints is read from its output, and for each component it prints as `unknown` the record pastes the command and output that read the source INV-6 names for that component, or, while that source has no entry for the task, says so and pastes the reading of the interim record the orchestrator used in its place. S1 (plan 006: the same finding class three times on one artifact, from any reviewer) is decided from the record's finding-class table, which gives a class to every finding the PR-feedback sweep lists, whatever its disposition, and to every task-level audit finding; three rows of one class stop the artifact. Read that table over non-advisory rows only: list advisory P2 rows with their classes (`advisory-p2` and the `local:<sha7>:<n>` rows `local-advisory.sh` writes), exclude them from S1's three-rows count, and name the excluded rows in the record. The gate's S6 check still sees every ledger row, so an advisory class at three rows gets its `searches` entry from `acceptance-front-matter.py` like any other. INV-6's message and head counts and the S2 lines (`revises`, `amendments`, `questions`, `bot_p1_heads`) take no ledger rows; `scripts/regime-counters.sh` prints them unchanged.
- A change to a rule sentence requested of a worker travels as a task amendment (hashed, checked by `scripts/orchestrator/task-consistency-check.py` (C1 to C10 and C7b) before dispatch and at acceptance, confirmed by the review seat), never as a PONG answer.
- When a finding class reaches three on one artifact (the record's ledger) or `scripts/regime-counters.sh` prints an S1 candidate, the next acceptance action is the records search for that class, pasted into the record as the line `search: <class> -> <the matching mistake records or none>`, and the matching correction is applied when its mechanism is landed, or landed first when it is pending, mechanism by mechanism, before any dispatch; a class is a slug of `[a-z0-9-]` assigned at disposition time, never text taken from a review title. `scripts/orchestrator/three-repeat.sh <class>` validates the slug, runs the records search and the CompactionDB search without a shell and prints the line. The gate (`scripts/require-crit-review.py`, S6) refuses the merge for a ledger class at three or more rows whose `searches` entry does not equal the mistake records naming the class; `acceptance-front-matter.py` writes the entry from the same lookup. Pasting the `search:` line and applying the correction before any dispatch remain the orchestrator's rule. - At regime or session boundaries, write pending acceptance records, then mechanically commit every `.orchestration` file so no untracked tail remains. Lessons from a session are codified in this repository (a rule, the skill, or a check) through a task; Claude auto-memory is not a durable store for regime procedure. The canonical clone is pull and apply only and untouched by any seat: no edits, no apply from a dirty tree (the run_before guard refuses it), and one orchestrator identity per repository, seated at the working clone.
- Stop checklist, at every regime or session boundary and in this order: write pending acceptance records; mask every `.orchestration` file the boundary commit adds or changes with `uv run --no-project --with pyyaml scripts/validate-agent-assets.py --mask-secrets <files>`, which also normalises home directories to `~`; run `make validate-agent-assets` (real exit status); make the `.orchestration` boundary commit with zero untracked tail on a fresh `orchestration/boundary-<YYYY-MM-DD>` branch from `origin/main` and merge its PR with `gh pr merge --squash --auto`, queued only while no other PR is between its final head and its merge (plan 020 step 3; otherwise the boundary PR waits and is merged after that PR); remove every worker with `herdr-agents --remove-worker <worktree>` (despawn, delivery off, leave, tab or workspace closed); check stale identities with `identities.sh <path> <type>` (exactly one name at the main checkout, none at a worker worktree); close Crit review servers (`pgrep -f 'crit _serve'` must be empty); in a CompactionDB-opted-in project, review `uv run --no-project .claude/hooks/contextdb_cli.py memory candidates --limit 20` and promote each candidate worth keeping with `uv run --no-project .claude/hooks/contextdb_cli.py memory promote <id> --scope project`, or leave it. The orchestrator workspace itself stays resident for the next session unless the operator restarts the machine. `make check-regime-boundary` (`scripts/check-regime-boundary.sh`) checks this list and the orchestrator seat lock, one line per violation.
- Before every `.orchestration` boundary commit, run the masker on the files it adds or changes (`uv run --no-project --with pyyaml scripts/validate-agent-assets.py --mask-secrets <files>`), then `make validate-agent-assets`, and branch on its real exit status, never through a pipe; fix a failure before pushing, because committed audit evidence can trip the secret scan, which also rejects a home directory path in `.orchestration/**`.
- The orchestrator never pushes a repository change to `main` directly. `main` is protected by the GitHub ruleset "main integration gate": a pull request is required, review threads must be resolved, the seven required checks must pass under the strict up-to-date policy, and `main` cannot be deleted or rewound. The `.orchestration` boundary commit goes on a fresh branch from `origin/main`, `orchestration/boundary-<YYYY-MM-DD>` (suffix `-2`, `-3`, … for another boundary the same day, since merged branches are kept), opens as a PR, and is merged with `gh pr merge --squash --auto`: each required job decides inside itself and reports success on an `.orchestration`-only diff; a skipped required job would report Success (fail-open), so no required job carries a job-level `if` or a `needs`. An acceptance merge happens only on GitHub using step 10.5; a local merge followed by a push is no longer a path.
- For CompactionDB-opted-in projects, verify during the sync that every accepted task has a consolidated decision record.

  - Pair form, in the pair workspace's dedicated audit tab: `herdr-agents --audit <head-sha> --task <id> [--out <path>] <main DIR>`. It writes `.orchestration/validation/<id>-audit-<sha7>.md` and codex's final message to that file's `.last.md` companion, whose last non-blank line is the verdict.

    - The gate needs both the transcript file and its non-empty `.last.md` companion.

  - A new push, including a `gh pr update-branch` merge, needs a new audit of the new head.

   107	5. **出力と予約の同一性** 名前には 40 桁の head を使う（7 桁で衝突させない）。lock は信頼ルート配下の固定 inode に O_EXCL で作り、置換を inode 比較で検出する。物理スロット 1 つに lock 1 つ。
   108	6. **正直な残余** 境界だけが緩和するリスクを `closed` と書かない。各文は残余を 1 行で明記する。
   109	0. **脅威モデル（D-024-21）** 席は同じ OS ユーザで動き、ホストは席間の信頼境界ではない（同一 UID のプロセスは symlink 差し替え、共有 `.git` の object 差し替え、hook の子プロセス、Herdr socket 経由の host 実行で、ホスト内のどの検査も迂回できる）。regime の硬い境界は GitHub（保護された main、必須チェック、orchestrator の identity によるマージ）。ただしこの境界は **worker 席が orchestrator の GitHub 資格情報を共有しない**ときだけ成立する（D-024-22：worker 席は専用の GitHub identity（別アカウントまたは App のトークン）で `gh` に login し、ruleset の bypass 一覧に入らない。orchestrator の keychain トークンを worker の config dir に持ち込まない。identity が分かれるまで「GitHub が境界」は未成立と書く）。**同一 macOS ユーザでは資格情報は分離できない**（gh は keychain の項目を host/user で引き、同じ UID の gh は orchestrator のトークンを読める。`GH_CONFIG_DIR` は設定を分けるだけ）。防止には worker 席を別の OS ユーザ（または別ホスト）で動かすしかなく、それは D-024-23 の将来項目（P1-16、操作者の判断）。それまで GitHub 境界は **検知**で守る：記録は boundary の記録 PR まで main に無いので、検知は次の記録 PR の regime ジョブで行う（`.orchestration/acceptance/**` に触れる PR で、前回 boundary 以降の main の各マージ commit に、gate 通過の証跡を持つ受け入れ記録が対応することを検査し、無ければその PR を失敗させる；P1-11 owner a02 の行 `ci:detection:1`）。main push 時点の検知は記録が無いので不可能であり、文は「次の記録 PR で検知、防止ではない」と書く。悪意ある worker に耐えるべき入力（承認台帳、gate が読む証跡 of record）は GitHub から sha 指定で API 経由（sandbox 内）に読み、ローカルファイルやローカル object database からは読まない。ホスト内の制御（本節 1〜10）は事故と prompt injection による損害の抑制であり、文はそう書く。
   110	8. **承認はコミット済み台帳から読む** permission の決定行（`scope=permission approved_by=user diff_sha256=…`）は anchored checkout の作業コピーではなく、コミット済みの台帳から読む。読み方は `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` が返す commit sha を取り、GitHub API（`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/.orchestration/decisions.tsv?ref=<sha>`、sandbox 内）でその sha の内容を取得する。ローカルの `git show` は共有 object database が書けるため中間 tree の差し替えで偽物を返しうる（第 3 回審査の所見 2）（ローカルの ref 名 `origin/main` は経由しない。`refs/replace/` も書けるので replacement を無効にする。Codex worker は `.git/objects` と `.git/refs` に書けるので ref は差し替えられるが、sha で指した object は内容アドレスで偽造できない）。作業コピーの行は提案で、記録 PR が main にマージされて初めて承認になる（PR の承認は操作者の操作）。偽造には main へのマージが要る。 The same applies to the PR content a mechanism evaluates (the verdict, the audit precheck, the counters): the changeset is read from GitHub at the 40-hex head (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/<base40>...<head40>`, `…/contents/<path>?ref=<head40>`) or from a private clone whose object store no worker can write; the main checkout's shared `.git/objects` and its `origin/main` ref are not evidence sources, because Codex workers write them (a04 C-80 round 1, 2026-10-19). Evidence files are named and matched by the full 40-hex head, never by a 7-character prefix. A mechanism whose application path runs code this contract does not yet cover (the agmsg storage layer sourced by `dispatch.sh`/`history.sh`; the integration gate until its own hardening task lands) names that task as the prerequisite of its `--apply` mode and runs shadow-only until the prerequisite is merged. The sha of canonical `main` comes from the fixed repository's API (`gh api repos/mryfmo/dotfiles/git/ref/heads/main --jq .object.sha`), never from `git ls-remote origin`, whose destination the local remote and URL-rewrite configuration control (P1-12 a04 C-80, 2026-10-19T20:01Z); the content read at that sha comes from `repos/mryfmo/dotfiles/contents/<path>?ref=<sha40>`. Every `gh api` call that decides also binds the host with `--hostname github.com` (`GH_HOST` and the hosts configuration select the API host otherwise), a subcommand binds it through the `github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles` form of `--repo`, and a test that exports a hostile `GH_HOST` shows the call still names github.com or refuses (a02 review b2a186e, 2026-10-19T20:36Z).
   111	9. **私設キャッシュ** orchestrator 側の実行は worker と共有するキャッシュ（`~/.cache/uv`、`~/.local/share/uv`、mise）から実行可能物を読まない。`UV_CACHE_DIR` を anchored checkout 配下（`.agents/worklog/uv-cache`、gitignored、worker 書き込み不可）に固定し、`uv run --no-config --no-project --offline --python <信頼ルートの絶対パスのインタプリタ>` で起動する（`--no-config` で uv の設定探索を止め、`--python` の絶対パスで cwd や親の `.venv` の発見を止める；敵対的な `.venv` と `uv.toml` を置いた fixture で検証）。hook は uv を使わず jq と python 標準ライブラリだけで動く。 One trusted interpreter resolver (`scripts/orchestrator/trusted-interpreter.sh`, P1-3 lineage) resolves `<abs>` from the repository's pinned declaration to a regular file under the tool manager's install root (the install root is anchored to the passwd home of the real uid, never to the HOME variable, which a caller can forge), refuses anything else, and every orchestrator-side script consumes it; no script keeps its own `command -v`, `mise which` or PATH fallback (ci-rerun.sh security review 44cb835, 2026-10-19). Shell code of other projects (the agmsg storage layer and its `drivers.partition` sourcing) is never sourced by an orchestrator-side mechanism; counters are read from the agmsg SQLite store read-only with a fixed query or from the pasted record. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-a6baa1c.md:582:   236	   The trusted entrypoint fixes the absolute paths for Bash, uv, Python, gh, git, jq and required utilities before reading PR-controlled input. It executes verified realpaths without rediscovery. The repository's Python declaration is a read-only input; consume `scripts/orchestrator/trusted-interpreter.sh` from the authenticated trusted base when present. The P1-3 resolver alone resolves the pinned declaration to a regular executable file under the tool manager's install root, anchored to the passwd home of the real uid, never to HOME, and outside worktrees, worker-writable caches and `$TMPDIR`. A symlink spelling alone authenticates nothing. An absent resolver or invalid trusted installation holds rather than selecting another interpreter from PATH, mise, uv discovery or a checkout. No private resolver, `command -v` or `mise which` fallback is retained here. Refuse a missing, ambiguous or malformed passwd result, or any disagreement between that passwd home and HOME, with exit 2 and a named `trusted-interpreter:` diagnostic before selecting a candidate. Derive the installation root only as `<passwd home>/.local/share/mise/installs`, never from the HOME variable, and construct only `<install root>/python/<version>/bin/python3`. Require an executable regular file after `realpath`, within the expected protected installation, outside the worktree, manifest worker roots, worker-writable caches and `$TMPDIR`. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-a6baa1c.md:2737:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:113:On success print exactly one absolute interpreter realpath and exit 0. On every refusal print exactly one line `trusted-interpreter: refused: <code>` to stderr, print no interpreter on stdout, and exit 2. The codes are `dirty-environment`, `script-path`, `home-mismatch`, `declaration-missing`, `declaration-malformed`, `declaration-duplicate`, `install-missing`, `install-not-regular`, `install-symlink`, `install-outside-root` and `version-mismatch`. Invalid entry environment uses `dirty-environment`; a noncanonical or symlinked script path uses `script-path`; invalid passwd data or HOME disagreement uses `home-mismatch`. An absent declaration uses `declaration-missing`, duplicates use `declaration-duplicate`, and malformed, non-exact or metacharacter-bearing declarations use `declaration-malformed`. An absent candidate uses `install-missing`, a non-executable or non-regular candidate uses `install-not-regular`, a symlinked installation uses `install-symlink`, a forbidden resolved path uses `install-outside-root`, and a resolved installation version differing from the pin uses `version-mismatch`. Every negative test asserts its specific reason code as well as exit 2 and no interpreter stdout; an earlier refusal is not coverage of a later check. There is no `command -v`, `mise which`, PATH search, version-alias selection, download or fallback. Do not execute a candidate to discover whether it is trustworthy.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-a6baa1c.md:2738:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:119:Apply the same trusted-parent clean prefix, privileged program entry, exact environment verification, canonical `$0` realpath check and real-uid passwd-home match to `scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh`. Refuse any entry failure with exit 2 and exactly one `ci-rerun: refused: <code>` line before tool setup or effects: `dirty-environment` for invalid environment names or values, `script-path` for a noncanonical or symlinked script path, and `home-mismatch` for invalid passwd data or HOME disagreement. Do not repair the environment or self re-exec. .orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-0512275.md:2779:.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-0512275.md:385:Item 2: “A shell script that runs under a PR-controlled or worker-controlled environment (verdict.sh, the chain glue, CI steps) is executed as a program with `#!/bin/bash -p`, never as `bash <file>`: privileged mode discards inherited functions, `BASH_ENV`/`ENV`, `SHELLOPTS`, `BASHOPTS`, `CDPATH` and `GLOBIGNORE` before the first statement, and the first statement re-executes the program under `/usr/bin/env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME="$HOME" LANG=C.UTF-8 /bin/bash --noprofile --norc -p "$0" "$@"` (long options before `-p`: bash exits 2 otherwise) unless its environment already consists of exactly the allowed names, checked through absolute paths (`/usr/bin/env`, `/usr/bin/grep`) under `-p`; a caller-set sentinel variable is not a sanitization proof, because the caller controls it (a04 C-80 round 1, 2026-10-19); sanitization performed by later statements (unset -f, compgen, PATH edits) is not a boundary, because the statements themselves resolve through the untrusted names (PR #410 security reviews 513e5d0 and 6b7e783, 2026-10-19).” “No script accepts a caller-supplied executable directory; interpreters are the fixed absolute paths item 9 names.” “Python は `-I`。” “PATH 探索で実行するものは無い。”
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-0512275.md:2780:.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-0512275.md:393:Add executable `scripts/orchestrator/trusted-interpreter.sh`, with English shdoc comments and `#!/bin/bash -p`. Execute it as a program; do not source it or invoke it as `bash <file>`. Its first statement implements the quoted environment check and re-exec, before assignments, traps, tool discovery or declaration reads. Check the actual environment through absolute paths; a caller-provided sentinel is not proof. The clean invocation must terminate normally rather than repeatedly re-execing because Bash maintains its own environment entries.

**無害化した環境を最初に** 最初の処理として `env -i` に入り、PATH は信頼ルートで解決した絶対バイナリへのリンクだけの私設ディレクトリ（shims、空、相対は拒否）。git は毎回 `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always` と明示 `-C`（https だけ許す。`protocol.allow=never` 単独は必要な fetch を止める）。 検査の読み取りは `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` で部分クローンの遅延 fetch（checkout 設定の credential.helper を起動しうる）を止め、`-c submodule.recurse=false --ignore-submodules=all` で submodule 内の status/diff（submodule 自身の設定が filter を有効化しうる）を止める。`.gitmodules` を持つ checkout は検査対象として拒否する。 `-C` は作業木を束縛しないので（repo-local の `core.worktree` が読み先を checkout 外へ向けられる）、git は `--git-dir=<checkout>/.git --work-tree=<checkout>` を明示し、`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` の realpath が checkout と一致しないときは拒否する。 premise や検査の「コマンド実行」は、固定語彙の読み取り専用プローブ（`git rev-parse <ref>`、`test -e <path>`、`grep -c <pattern> <file>` のように検査器自身が解釈する形）だけを許し、任意のシェル文字列は実行しない（本文のハッシュはコマンド文を認証するだけで、`python -I scripts/x.py` のファイル被演算子や `source ./x.sh` の中身は認証しない）。diff と show は `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` と `-c core.attributesFile=/dev/null -c core.sshCommand=false` を付け、PR 側の `.gitattributes`（external diff、textconv、filter）が検査内容や実行物を変えないようにする。Python は `-I`。PATH 探索で実行するものは無い。 A shell script that runs under a PR-controlled or worker-controlled environment (verdict.sh, the chain glue, CI steps) is executed as a program with `#!/bin/bash -p`, never as `bash <file>`: privileged mode discards inherited functions, `BASH_ENV`/`ENV`, `SHELLOPTS`, `BASHOPTS`, `CDPATH` and `GLOBIGNORE` before the first bash exits 2 otherwise) unless its environment already consists of exactly the allowed names, checked through absolute paths (`/usr/bin/env`, `/usr/bin/grep`) under `-p`; a caller-set sentinel variable is not a sanitization proof, because the caller controls it (a04 C-80 round 1, 2026-10-19); sanitization performed by later statements (unset -f, compgen, PATH edits) is not a boundary, because the statements themselves resolve through the untrusted names (PR #410 security reviews 513e5d0 and 6b7e783, 2026-10-19). No script accepts a caller-supplied executable directory; interpreters are the fixed absolute paths item 9 names.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-0512275.md:2807:.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-0512275.md:1472:110-8. **承認はコミット済み台帳から読む** permission の決定行（`scope=permission approved_by=user diff_sha256=…`）は anchored checkout の作業コピーではなく、コミット済みの台帳から読む。読み方は `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` が返す commit sha を取り、GitHub API（`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/contents/.orchestration/decisions.tsv?ref=<sha>`、sandbox 内）でその sha の内容を取得する。ローカルの `git show` は共有 object database が書けるため中間 tree の差し替えで偽物を返しうる（第 3 回審査の所見 2）（ローカルの ref 名 `origin/main` は経由しない。`refs/replace/` も書けるので replacement を無効にする。Codex worker は `.git/objects` と `.git/refs` に書けるので ref は差し替えられるが、sha で指した object は内容アドレスで偽造できない）。作業コピーの行は提案で、記録 PR が main にマージされて初めて承認になる（PR の承認は操作者の操作）。偽造には main へのマージが要る。 The same applies to the PR content a mechanism evaluates (the verdict, the audit precheck, the counters): the changeset is read from GitHub at the 40-hex head (`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/compare/<base40>...<head40>`, `…/contents/<path>?ref=<head40>`) or from a private clone whose object store no worker can write; the main checkout's shared `.git/objects` and its `origin/main` ref are not evidence sources, because Codex workers write them (a04 C-80 round 1, 2026-10-19). Evidence files are named and matched by the full 40-hex head, never by a 7-character prefix.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-0512275.md:2808:.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-0512275.md:2036:2. **無害化した環境を最初に** 最初の処理として `env -i` に入り、PATH は信頼ルートで解決した絶対バイナリへのリンクだけの私設ディレクトリ（shims、空、相対は拒否）。git は毎回 `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c protocol.allow=never -c protocol.https.allow=always` と明示 `-C`（https だけ許す。`protocol.allow=never` 単独は必要な fetch を止める）。 検査の読み取りは `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` で部分クローンの遅延 fetch（checkout 設定の credential.helper を起動しうる）を止め、`-c submodule.recurse=false --ignore-submodules=all` で submodule 内の status/diff（submodule 自身の設定が filter を有効化しうる）を止める。`.gitmodules` を持つ checkout は検査対象として拒否する。 `-C` は作業木を束縛しないので（repo-local の `core.worktree` が読み先を checkout 外へ向けられる）、git は `--git-dir=<checkout>/.git --work-tree=<checkout>` を明示し、`git rev-parse --show-toplevel` の realpath が checkout と一致しないときは拒否する。 premise や検査の「コマンド実行」は、固定語彙の読み取り専用プローブ（`git rev-parse <ref>`、`test -e <path>`、`grep -c <pattern> <file>` のように検査器自身が解釈する形）だけを許し、任意のシェル文字列は実行しない（本文のハッシュはコマンド文を認証するだけで、`python -I scripts/x.py` のファイル被演算子や `source ./x.sh` の中身は認証しない）。diff と show は `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` と `-c core.attributesFile=/dev/null -c core.sshCommand=false` を付け、PR 側の `.gitattributes`（external diff、textconv、filter）が検査内容や実行物を変えないようにする。Python は `-I`。PATH 探索で実行するものは無い。 A shell script that runs under a PR-controlled or worker-controlled environment (verdict.sh, the chain glue, CI steps) is executed as a program with `#!/bin/bash -p`, never as `bash <file>`: privileged mode discards inherited functions, `BASH_ENV`/`ENV`, `SHELLOPTS`, `BASHOPTS`, `CDPATH` and `GLOBIGNORE` before the first statement, and the first statement re-executes the program under `/usr/bin/env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME="$HOME" LANG=C.UTF-8 /bin/bash --noprofile --norc -p "$0" "$@"` (long options before `-p`: bash exits 2 otherwise) unless its environment already consists of exactly the allowed names, checked through absolute paths (`/usr/bin/env`, `/usr/bin/grep`) under `-p`; a caller-set sentinel variable is not a sanitization proof, because the caller controls it (a04 C-80 round 1, 2026-10-19); sanitization performed by later statements (unset -f, compgen, PATH edits) is not a boundary, because the statements themselves resolve through the untrusted names (PR #410 security reviews 513e5d0 and 6b7e783, 2026-10-19). No script accepts a caller-supplied executable directory; interpreters are the fixed absolute paths item 9 names.

.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-82ced8f.md:3068:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:101:Item 9: “orchestrator 側の実行は worker と共有するキャッシュ（`~/.cache/uv`、`~/.local/share/uv`、mise）から実行可能物を読まない。” “`UV_CACHE_DIR` を anchored checkout 配下（`.agents/worklog/uv-cache`、gitignored、worker 書き込み不可）に固定し、`uv run --no-config --no-project --offline --python <信頼ルートの絶対パスのインタプリタ>` で起動する（`--no-config` で uv の設定探索を止め、`--python` の絶対パスで cwd や親の `.venv` の発見を止める；敵対的な `.venv` と `uv.toml` を置いた fixture で検証）。” “One trusted interpreter resolver (`scripts/orchestrator/trusted-interpreter.sh`, P1-3 lineage) resolves `<abs>` from the repository's pinned declaration to a regular file under the tool manager's install root (the install root is anchored to the passwd home of the real uid, never to the HOME variable, which a caller can forge), refuses anything else, and every orchestrator-side script consumes it; no script keeps its own `command -v`, `mise which` or PATH fallback (ci-rerun.sh security review 44cb835, 2026-10-19).”
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-82ced8f.md:3069:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:117:## Item 2 — consume the resolver in ci-rerun.sh
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-82ced8f.md:3070:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:119:Apply the same trusted-parent clean prefix, privileged program entry, exact environment verification, canonical `$0` realpath check and real-uid passwd-home match to `scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh`. Refuse any entry failure with exit 2 and exactly one `ci-rerun: refused: <code>` line before tool setup or effects: `dirty-environment` for invalid environment names or values, `script-path` for a noncanonical or symlinked script path, and `home-mismatch` for invalid passwd data or HOME disagreement. Do not repair the environment or self re-exec. Invoke the resolver by its bound absolute realpath through the same clean prefix, supplying HOME from the verified passwd home, and consume its single validated result; propagate refusal without trying another interpreter.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-82ced8f.md:3071:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:127:Before reading or writing the flake registry, ledger or reservation state, resolve `.github/flakes.yaml`, `.orchestration/validation/ci-reruns.tsv` and the reservation parent `.orchestration/validation/ci-reruns.lock.d` with `realpath`. Require the registry and ledger to be regular files and the reservation parent to be a directory under the confirmed repository root, outside manifest worker roots, worker-writable caches and `$TMPDIR`. Refuse symlinks in the destination or any path component below that root, and, on a case-insensitive filesystem, a destination differing from its declared pathname only by case. Use only the validated canonical destinations for subsequent reads and effects. Apply the same checks to an existing per-run reservation directory before inspecting its claim and to a newly claimed directory before using it. Missing output objects may be created only at the existing effect point after validating their existing parent chain and resolving the intended destination; resolve and type-check each newly created object before appending ledger data or using a claim. Preserve atomic per-run creation and never replace an existing object during validation. Any destination-validation failure exits 2 with exactly one `ci-rerun: refused: <code>` line before registry parsing, ledger access or a rerun, leaving redirected targets unchanged. Destination codes are `destination-outside-root` for a resolved path outside the confirmed repository or in a forbidden root, `destination-symlink` for an otherwise contained path with a symlink in the destination or its parent chain, `destination-case-alias` for an otherwise contained case alias, `destination-not-regular` for an invalid registry or ledger file type, and `destination-not-directory` for an invalid reservation directory type. Check containment before symlink, case-alias and type checks so an outside-root mutation has its own distinguishable code.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04-text-security-82ced8f.md:3072:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:155:Add these tests to `tests/unit/test_ci_rerun.py::CiRerunTest`. Each destination test starts from an accepted baseline: a temporary copy of the repository tree whose own `scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh` is executed as the program through the trusted-parent clean prefix. The copy must be the program's confirmed repository root, with its registry, ledger and reservation paths accepted; make one positive assertion of exit 0 and the expected fixture-only behavior first. The CI runner provisions these temporary copies outside the forbidden worker/cache/tmp roots, using the real pinned installation read-only; the sandboxed worker records blocked local evidence when that baseline is unavailable. Executing the original script against paths in another temporary tree is not an accepted baseline.

Under C-88, the following verbatim sentences are normative; the design path supplies context rather than replacing these requirements.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3043:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:99:Item 2: “A shell script that runs under a PR-controlled or worker-controlled environment (verdict.sh, the chain glue, CI steps) is executed as a program with `#!/bin/bash -p`, never as `bash <file>`, and only by a trusted parent that supplies the clean environment before the exec: `/usr/bin/env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=<passwd home> LANG=C.UTF-8 /bin/bash --noprofile --norc -p <absolute script path> …` (long options before `-p`). Privileged mode discards inherited functions, `BASH_ENV`/`ENV`, `SHELLOPTS`, `BASHOPTS`, `CDPATH` and `GLOBIGNORE`, but on Linux an inherited `LD_PRELOAD`/`LD_AUDIT` already executes while the loader maps `/bin/bash`, before `-p` or any statement runs, so a self re-exec inside the script is not a boundary and re-executing `"$0"` would reopen the caller's pathname (a worker-owned symlink can be swapped between the two executions); the program therefore verifies and refuses instead of repairing: its environment must consist of exactly the allowed names (checked through absolute paths `/usr/bin/env`, `/usr/bin/grep`), `$0` resolved with `realpath` must be a regular file under the repository root, and HOME must equal the passwd home of the real uid (`/usr/bin/dscl . -read /Users/<user> NFSHomeDirectory` on macOS, `/usr/bin/getent passwd <uid>` on Linux), otherwise exit 2 with a named message. A caller-set sentinel variable is not a sanitization proof, because the caller controls it (ci-efficiency a04 and verdict a04 C-80 reviews, 2026-10-19). No script accepts a caller-supplied executable directory; interpreters are the fixed absolute paths item 9 names.” “Python は `-I`。” “PATH 探索で実行するものは無い。”
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3044:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:111:Before traps, tool discovery or declaration reads, verify the actual environment's exact allowed names through `/usr/bin/env` and `/usr/bin/grep`, the fixed PATH and LANG values, the script's absolute realpath and the passwd-home match. Account explicitly for Bash's own maintained environment entries so the clean prefix succeeds; allow no sanitization sentinel or production test exemption. Require `$0` to be the bound absolute canonical script pathname and its realpath to be a regular file under the trusted repository root, outside worker roots; refuse a symlinked `$0`, including a worker-owned symlink to the trusted script, without reopening it. Any invalid environment, script path or HOME exits 2 with a named `trusted-interpreter:` diagnostic and no stdout, instead of repairing or re-executing.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3045:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:115:Obtain the real uid through `/usr/bin/id -ru`. On macOS obtain its user name through `/usr/bin/id -run` and its passwd home through `/usr/bin/dscl . -read /Users/<user> NFSHomeDirectory`; on Linux use `/usr/bin/getent passwd <uid>`. Refuse a missing, ambiguous or malformed passwd result, or any disagreement between that passwd home and HOME, with exit 2 and a named `trusted-interpreter:` diagnostic before selecting a candidate. Derive the installation root only as `<passwd home>/.local/share/mise/installs`, never from the HOME variable, and construct only `<install root>/python/<version>/bin/python3`. Resolve and validate the candidate before printing it. Require an executable regular file after `realpath`, within the expected protected installation, outside the worktree, manifest worker roots, worker-writable caches and `$TMPDIR`. Check resolved path boundaries, including filesystem case behavior where applicable. Refuse a symlinked installation rather than accepting a redirected install directory.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3046:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:117:On success print exactly one absolute interpreter realpath and exit 0. On every refusal print exactly one line `trusted-interpreter: refused: <code>` to stderr, print no interpreter on stdout, and exit 2. The codes are `dirty-environment`, `script-path`, `home-mismatch`, `declaration-missing`, `declaration-malformed`, `declaration-duplicate`, `install-missing`, `install-not-regular`, `install-symlink`, `install-outside-root` and `version-mismatch`. Invalid entry environment uses `dirty-environment`; a noncanonical or symlinked script path uses `script-path`; invalid passwd data or HOME disagreement uses `home-mismatch`. An absent declaration uses `declaration-missing`, duplicates use `declaration-duplicate`, and malformed, non-exact or metacharacter-bearing declarations use `declaration-malformed`. An absent candidate uses `install-missing`, a non-executable or non-regular candidate uses `install-not-regular`, a symlinked installation uses `install-symlink`, a forbidden resolved path uses `install-outside-root`, and a resolved installation version differing from the pin uses `version-mismatch`. Every negative test asserts its specific reason code as well as exit 2 and no interpreter stdout; an earlier refusal is not coverage of a later check. There is no `command -v`, `mise which`, PATH search, version-alias selection, download or fallback. Do not execute a candidate to discover whether it is trustworthy.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3047:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:123:Apply the same trusted-parent clean prefix, privileged program entry, exact environment verification, canonical `$0` realpath check and real-uid passwd-home match to `scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh`. Refuse any entry failure with exit 2 and exactly one `ci-rerun: refused: <code>` line before tool setup or effects: `dirty-environment` for invalid environment names or values, `script-path` for a noncanonical or symlinked script path, and `home-mismatch` for invalid passwd data or HOME disagreement. Do not repair the environment or self re-exec. Invoke the resolver by its bound absolute realpath through the same clean prefix, supplying HOME from the verified passwd home, and consume its single validated result; propagate refusal without trying another interpreter.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3048:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:125:Remove Python from the old tool-discovery loop, including the line-45 fallback and line-47 shims test. Do not retain or recreate those mechanisms elsewhere. Bind non-Python tools from explicit protected installation locations, using their validated realpaths or a private fixed PATH of links to those realpaths; caller PATH entries never populate that directory. Missing trusted tools fail closed.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3049:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:127:Every external command, including cleanup on early failure and the environment, passwd-home and script-realpath checks, uses an absolute path or the fixed PATH established after entry verification. Keep the EXIT trap’s `/bin/rm` and cover both successful execution and refusal before tool setup completes. Apply the relevant section-5.14 Git invocation controls to the existing root-discovery probe; do not introduce new Git probes or arbitrary shell-command inputs.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3050:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:129:Entry verification must refuse any `GIT_*` name in the program's environment, including `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, before invoking Git. The trusted-parent clean prefix must remove them before exec. Confirm that the existing root-discovery probe returns the canonical trusted repository root bound to the script location; a repository-local `core.worktree` redirection must cause exit 2 with `ci-rerun: refused: repository-root`, rather than selecting another root or silently overriding the redirection. Confirm the root before deriving the registry, ledger or reservation paths.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3051:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:133:Before reading or writing the flake registry, ledger or reservation state, resolve `.github/flakes.yaml`, `.orchestration/validation/ci-reruns.tsv` and the reservation parent `.orchestration/validation/ci-reruns.lock.d` with `realpath`. Require the registry and ledger to be regular files and the reservation parent to be a directory under the confirmed repository root, outside manifest worker roots, worker-writable caches and `$TMPDIR`. Refuse symlinks in the destination or any path component below that root, and, on a case-insensitive filesystem, a destination differing from its declared pathname only by case. Use only the validated canonical destinations for subsequent reads and effects. Apply the same checks to an existing per-run reservation directory before inspecting its claim and to a newly claimed directory before using it. Missing output objects may be created only at the existing effect point after validating their existing parent chain and resolving the intended destination; resolve and type-check each newly created object before appending ledger data or using a claim. Preserve atomic per-run creation and never replace an existing object during validation. Any destination-validation failure exits 2 with exactly one `ci-rerun: refused: <code>` line before registry parsing, ledger access or a rerun, leaving redirected targets unchanged. Destination codes are `destination-outside-root` for a resolved path outside the confirmed repository or in a forbidden root, `destination-symlink` for an otherwise contained path with a symlink in the destination or its parent chain, `destination-case-alias` for an otherwise contained case alias, `destination-not-regular` for an invalid registry or ledger file type, and `destination-not-directory` for an invalid reservation directory type. Check containment before symlink, case-alias and type checks so an outside-root mutation has its own distinguishable code.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3052:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:145:Write the failing regressions before the fix and paste red and green output. Every negative security case asserts its specific refusal code, not just exit 2 or an empty marker. Declaration-mutating negative cases (missing, malformed, duplicate, non-exact and metacharacter-bearing declarations, and the exact declaration used for a missing installation) execute the canonical resolver in a temporary copy of the repository tree through the trusted-parent clean prefix. Mutate only that copy's declaration; keep the real uid's passwd-home installation read-only and retain the real passwd-home lookup and install-root anchor. Add `tests/unit/test_trusted_interpreter.py` with class `TrustedInterpreterTest` and these tests:
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3053:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:147:- `test_pinned_interpreter_ignores_checkout_path_without_mise`: prepend a temporary checkout’s marker-writing `.venv/bin/python3` to PATH with mise unavailable; direct dirty entry exits 2 with `trusted-interpreter: refused: dirty-environment` and no marker. Its positive clean-prefix case invokes the canonical resolver in the real repository, reads that repository’s pinned declaration and the tool-manager-installed interpreter beneath the real uid’s passwd-home install root read-only, and expects exactly one absolute realpath and exit 0. Assert that the printed path is an executable regular file under that install root, then execute it as `"<abs>" -I -c 'import sys; print(sys.version_info[:2])'` and compare the output with the pinned version’s major/minor pair. Assert the resolver exists before considering a skip: its red state is the refusal path, failing by absence before implementation. If the pinned installation is absent, skip only this positive case with the named reason `pinned-installation-unavailable`, including the pin and expected install root, and record the skip in `report.md` and `validation.md`; do not skip dirty-entry or other negative cases. An existing installation that fails validation or version matching is a test failure, not a skip; the marker remains absent in every case.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3054:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:150:- `test_duplicate_malformed_nonexact_or_metacharacter_declarations_are_refused`: through the clean prefix in the temporary repository copy, cover duplicate declarations with `trusted-interpreter: refused: declaration-duplicate`; malformed grammar, non-exact versions including `latest`, prefix or suffix lookalikes, and metacharacter-bearing values each assert `trusted-interpreter: refused: declaration-malformed`. Every case exits 2 with no interpreter stdout and no marker.
.orchestration/validation/dotfiles-T133-verdict-audit-pool-a04-text-security-c3c127c.md:3055:.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T133-ci-efficiency-followup-a04.md:152:- `test_program_entry_refuses_dirty_environment_or_symlinked_script`: invoke the program with exported functions, `BASH_ENV`/`ENV`, `LD_PRELOAD` and `LD_AUDIT` naming a marker-library path, planted PATH, a forged sanitization sentinel and a symlinked `$0`; dirty-entry cases assert `trusted-interpreter: refused: dirty-environment` and the symlinked-script case asserts `trusted-interpreter: refused: script-path`, each with exit 2, no interpreter stdout and no marker. The trusted-parent clean-prefix success assertion uses the read-only positive case above, with the real repository’s canonical script path and no marker. Verdict: correctFound one security issue in [PR #424](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/pull/424), head `44cb835`.

- **P1 · High confidence · `scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh:45` — The fallback still accepts a checkout-controlled interpreter from an activated virtualenv’s absolute PATH entry, leaving the owned interpreter-selection vulnerability open.**

  When `mise` is absent or cannot resolve `python3`, `command -v` can return `<checkout>/.venv/bin/python3`. Changing directory to `/` does not neutralize absolute PATH entries, and line 47 accepts this path because its directory is not named `shims`. The selected executable subsequently runs through uv and directly at line 162 with the operator’s authority; the latter retains the inherited environment, including any credentials.

  Resolve the fallback from explicitly trusted tool locations. Extend the regression test at `tests/unit/test_ci_rerun.py:273` with a marker-writing `python3` in `.venv/bin` **prepended to PATH**, with mise unavailable. The current fixture sets `VIRTUAL_ENV` but omits that activation behavior. This finding is based on code tracing, not an executed exploit.

Threat-table assessment:

| Rows | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Script and tests | Changes fit the owned interpreter-selection work, but the finding prevents closure. |
| Workflow/interpreter/environment inputs | **Insufficient mitigation:** excluding interpreter files from `allowed_files` does not prevent the helper from executing checkout-controlled files supplied through PATH. |
| Lint baseline | Unchanged; no baseline suppression introduced. |
| Task copy, metadata, separators | Local SHA-256 matches the report; correspondence with the original dispatch remains unverified. |
| Evidence records | Treated as untrusted claims; historical review receipts do not establish final-head correctness. |
| In-process effects | Test code installs a failing mise stub and fake gh; no live GitHub action is apparent in the fixtures. |
| New/renamed scripts | None introduced. |
| Merge, update-branch, forced removal | Procedural controls remain the orchestrator’s responsibility; this diff neither implements nor verifies their execution. |

No additional changeset-specific injection, unsafe deserialization, path-traversal, or authentication/authorization issue was identified. YAML continues to use `safe_load`; the earlier pre-pinning `env` and cleanup-command issues are fixed.

The parent itself must already be trusted and clean before starting `/usr/bin/env`; clearing the environment after a loader has consumed it is too late. There is no self re-exec.

Refuse a missing, ambiguous or malformed passwd result, or any disagreement between that passwd home and HOME, with exit 2 and a named `trusted-interpreter:` diagnostic before selecting a candidate. The codes are `dirty-environment`, `script-path`, `home-mismatch`, `declaration-missing`, `declaration-malformed`, `declaration-duplicate`, `install-missing`, `install-not-regular`, `install-symlink`, `install-outside-root` and `version-mismatch`. Invalid entry environment uses `dirty-environment`; a noncanonical or symlinked script path uses `script-path`; invalid passwd data or HOME disagreement uses `home-mismatch`. An absent declaration uses `declaration-missing`, duplicates use `declaration-duplicate`, and malformed, non-exact or metacharacter-bearing declarations use `declaration-malformed`. An absent candidate uses `install-missing`, a non-executable or non-regular candidate uses `install-not-regular`, a symlinked installation uses `install-symlink`, a forbidden resolved path uses `install-outside-root`, and a resolved installation version differing from the pin uses `version-mismatch`. Every negative test asserts its specific reason code as well as exit 2 and no interpreter stdout; an earlier refusal is not coverage of a later check. There is no `command -v`, `mise which`, PATH search, version-alias selection, download or fallback. Do not execute a candidate to discover whether it is trustworthy.

Verdict: correctFound one security issue in [PR #424](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/pull/424), head `44cb835`.

- **P1 · High confidence · `scripts/orchestrator/ci-rerun.sh:45` — The fallback still accepts a checkout-controlled interpreter from an activated virtualenv’s absolute PATH entry, leaving the owned interpreter-selection vulnerability open.**

  When `mise` is absent or cannot resolve `python3`, `command -v` can return `<checkout>/.venv/bin/python3`. Changing directory to `/` does not neutralize absolute PATH entries, and line 47 accepts this path because its directory is not named `shims`. The selected executable subsequently runs through uv and directly at line 162 with the operator’s authority; the latter retains the inherited environment, including any credentials.

  Resolve the fallback from explicitly trusted tool locations. Extend the regression test at `tests/unit/test_ci_rerun.py:273` with a marker-writing `python3` in `.venv/bin` **prepended to PATH**, with mise unavailable. The current fixture sets `VIRTUAL_ENV` but omits that activation behavior. This finding is based on code tracing, not an executed exploit.

Threat-table assessment:

| Rows | Assessment |
|---|---|
| Script and tests | Changes fit the owned interpreter-selection work, but the finding prevents closure. |
| Workflow/interpreter/environment inputs | **Insufficient mitigation:** excluding interpreter files from `allowed_files` does not prevent the helper from executing checkout-controlled files supplied through PATH. |
| Lint baseline | Unchanged; no baseline suppression introduced. |
| Task copy, metadata, separators | Local SHA-256 matches the report; correspondence with the original dispatch remains unverified. |
| Evidence records | Treated as untrusted claims; historical review receipts do not establish final-head correctness. |
| In-process effects | Test code installs a failing mise stub and fake gh; no live GitHub action is apparent in the fixtures. |
| New/renamed scripts | None introduced. |
| Merge, update-branch, forced removal | Procedural controls remain the orchestrator’s responsibility; this diff neither implements nor verifies their execution. |

No additional changeset-specific injection, unsafe deserialization, path-traversal, or authentication/authorization issue was identified. YAML continues to use `safe_load`; the earlier pre-pinning `env` and cleanup-command issues are fixed.

📝 まとめ: Pinned-head security review completed with one P1 finding; acceptance remains with the orchestrator.
Not checked: runtime tests, live CI, or dispatch provenance; filesystem access was read-only and the gh-first API request failed. The remaining risk is checkout-controlled execution with operator authority.

## Worker Playbook

1. Read the full `AGMSG-TASK v1` message.
2. Switch to the `repo` and read `task_file` before editing or running validations. Create the task branch without touching the shared `.git/config`, which is read-only for a Codex seat by design (T64 writable roots): `git switch -c <branch> --no-track origin/main`, push with `git push origin <branch>` (no `-u`), and open the PR as a draft with `gh pr create --draft --head <branch>`. Commit inside the sandbox, with `git -c commit.gpgsign=false` when the signing key is unreadable there; for a Claude seat only the push leaves the sandbox, and a Codex seat pushes from inside it (step 4). A Claude seat's sandbox can leave the same failed write behind, so it uses the same commands. A leftover `.git/config.lock` from a failed attempt is removed by the orchestrator. Remove a scratch worktree (for example one that proves a test fails on `origin/main`) with `git worktree remove <path>` only; never run `git worktree prune` from a sandboxed seat, because other worktrees' paths look missing inside the sandbox and prune then targets their admin directories in the shared `.git/worktrees`.
3. Treat `allowed_files` as the edit boundary. If it says to see the task file, read that section and follow it exactly.
4. Do not perform any `forbidden_actions`. Complete every command inside the sandbox and allowlist; never escalate an action outside that boundary for approval. Fail it instead, send `AGMSG-PONG v1 status=blocked` with the exact command and the boundary it crosses, and wait for the orchestrator to re-task. Agent-to-agent permission approval is forbidden: only the human operator answers a permission prompt. A Claude Code auto-mode classifier denial (for example Self-Modification) is such a boundary: stop without a diff, send `AGMSG-PONG v1 status=blocked` naming the classifier reason, and never pursue the same outcome through another tool. Fetch and fast-forward inside the sandbox; a public remote needs no credential. For Claude seats on macOS, Seatbelt denies the Mach lookup of `com.apple.trustd.agent`, so Go-based CLIs (`gh`, `gcloud`, `terraform`) fail TLS verification with `x509: OSStatus -26276` (`errSecInternal`); `git` uses Apple libcurl, LibreSSL and `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` and succeeds. On Linux, the bubblewrap sandbox denies the AF_UNIX keyring socket, so `gh` answers HTTP 401; `allowUnixSockets` cannot grant a path. Monitor and process visibility limits are in "Identity, delivery, and storage". On both platforms a Claude seat runs three commands outside the sandbox through the permission gate: `gh`, `git push`, and an authenticated `git fetch` (a private HTTPS remote, whose credential helper is `gh`); `excludedCommands` and `enableWeakerNetworkIsolation` are operator options, not selected alternatives. Look up a VERIFY item's external reference (upstream documentation, release notes, an API schema) with the WebFetch tool, not Bash `curl`. Three documented cases run outside the sandbox too: the task's main-checkout CompactionDB `memory add`, through the permission gate because that state directory is read-only from a worktree sandbox; writing the task's artifacts at their expected main-checkout paths and masking them with the repository masker, through the permission gate because the main checkout is not writable from a worktree sandbox; and `agmsg-dispatch`, through `excludedCommands` (step 11). Every other out-of-sandbox action stays a blocked PONG. A Codex seat has in-sandbox network (T64) and never leaves its sandbox.
5. Write artifacts to the exact expected paths (a Claude seat writes them through the permission gate, step 4). Do not invent alternate paths. A seat whose sandbox cannot write the main checkout (a Codex seat) writes them at the same relative paths in its own worktree, untracked, and the RESULT says so; the orchestrator moves them into the main checkout by absolute path before review. Worker-side review evidence carries a `-worker-` infix (`<task>-worker-crit.json`, `<task>-worker-review-receipt.md`), so it never collides with the orchestrator's own files.
6. Put the verbatim output of every validation command in `expected_validation_file`; every identifier your report claims to have created must appear in that output.
7. Put the isolation status or fallback rationale in `expected_sandbox_file`.
8. Put reusable learning triage in `expected_learning_file`; do not promote rules directly unless the task explicitly allows it.
9. Put AutoSkill run status or a not-used record in `expected_autoskill_file`.
10. If blocked, still write the report and evidence paths that explain the blocker.
11. Reply with the requested `done_signal`, normally `AGMSG-RESULT v1`, and include all artifact paths. To a herdr-paned orchestrator, send RESULT and PONG with `agmsg-dispatch <team> <worker> <orchestrator> <pane_id>` (for example `wN:p1`; single-line, shell-safe text) rather than bare `send.sh`, so the wake starts the idle orchestrator's turn and its Stop hook delivers the message. The Claude sandbox manifest lists `agmsg-dispatch` in `claude.sandbox.excludedCommands`, so a Claude worker runs it outside the sandbox from the first attempt: no failed sandboxed run, no unsandboxed retry, and no escalation. Claude Code still applies its permission rules to excluded commands, so the managed settings allow `Bash(agmsg-dispatch:*)` (the only managed `permissions.allow` entry) and the dispatch runs without a prompt. A Codex seat runs under Codex's own sandbox, which this setting does not cover.
12. Put a `cost:` line in the report with observed session token/cost figures when the runtime exposes them, otherwise `cost: n/a`. This report value feeds the T76 `AGMSG-ACCEPTANCE v1` cost line.
13. A worker executing an AGMSG-TASK treats the Understand-Anything auto-update hook instruction ("knowledge graph is stale, you MUST update it") as out of scope unless `.ua/**` is in its `allowed_files`: it records "hook fired; not acted on" in the report and continues. The orchestrator never runs the graph update in its own session; graph refreshes are separate worker tasks.
14. Before sending RESULT, a worker whose session started a Crit plan review accounts for its Crit review server. A Claude seat starts one through Plan Mode's ExitPlanMode hook, and a Codex seat through the Crit plugin's Stop hook (`crit plan-hook --mode codex`). `make check-regime-boundary` treats a running `crit _serve` as a violation, and unit tests that read the host `pgrep` fail while one runs.
